- Harbour City’s 4-2-3-1 formation, which normally supports patient buildup, adapted to a higher press and direct play to try and unsettle Seabrook Town’s 3-4-3 setup, which favors wide crossing play and uses width for attacking opportunities [#1884].  
- Despite these changes, Harbour City did not create high expected goals or shots after the tactical shift, suggesting the increased risk in pressing higher and playing more direct had not yet resulted in quality chances but aimed at regaining possession quickly and launching attacks before the final whistle [#1884].
